root_cause: Loss of secondary well barrier during workover. The cement plug was placed at approximately 1,000 m TVD — about 2,700 m above the perforated zone it was meant to isolate — in a 26-27 degree inclined section, using 254 gallons of 114 pcf slurry at a bottom-hole circulating temperature of 46 C. The plug was neither tagged nor pressure-tested, so the unset cement percolated and the slurry column behaved as a water column, lightening the hydrostatic head. The BOP was nippled down and the drill pipe pulled before the cement had fully set, removing the primary barrier. Gas percolated up the diluted brine column and the well became active and blew out within about 1.5 hours.
mitigation_applied: Well killed on 15 November 2020 after approximately 5.5 months uncontrolled; intervention included reinstating well control equipment, sustained water spraying to cool the wellhead, and drilling relief wells. SPE-206602-MS recommends placing two or three backup cement plugs together with kill fluid, or squeeze cementing before setting the abandonment plug, and monitoring sustained casing pressure (SCP), operator-imposed pressure (OIP) and thermal-induced pressure (TIP) periodically.

root_cause: Pipe became stuck at 2,727 m MD while drilling the 8.5 inch production hole, detected by a stretch test. The well subsequently lost control and blew out with a gas pressure of 281.2 kg/cm2. Suspected mechanisms for the initial stuck-up were differential pressure sticking, a water-swelling clay formation, or partial collapse of the wellbore.
mitigation_applied: Circulated brine to address the swelling-clay mechanism; checked for and cured lost circulation while keeping the hole full; attempted to identify casing leaks by measuring sustained casing pressure (SCP), operator-imposed pressure (OIP) and thermal-induced pressure (TIP). SPE-206602-MS notes that formation collapse of this kind can originate in plastic formations such as salt domes.

root_cause: Drilled into a depleted, micro-fractured sandstone where the formation fracture gradient fell below the hydrostatic mud column, initiating partial losses into the thief zone.
mitigation_applied: Mixed and spotted a 35 bbl LCM pill of nut plug and mica across the loss zone, soaked for two hours, and restored full circulation before drilling ahead.

root_cause: Top drive rotary bearing failure under sustained high-torque drilling; surface torque exceeded the make-up limit before the stall was detected.
mitigation_applied: Laid down and replaced the failed top drive assembly, re-established circulation, and resumed drilling only after a satisfactory functional test.

root_cause: Mud pump fluid-end washout during a high-rate circulation, causing a loss of standpipe pressure and an unscheduled flow interruption.
mitigation_applied: Repaired the damaged fluid end, pressure-tested the pump, and confirmed standpipe pressure before drilling ahead.

root_cause: Differential sticking: high hydrostatic overbalance embedded the drill collars in a thick filter cake across a permeable sand while the string was stationary.
mitigation_applied: Spotted a fresh-water soak pill across the stuck interval, worked the string free with jarring, and reduced mud weight to cut the differential overbalance.

root_cause: Formation pore pressure exceeded the active mud hydrostatic column when an overpressured sand stringer was penetrated, allowing formation gas to enter the wellbore.
mitigation_applied: Shut in the well on the annular preventer, recorded SIDPP and SICP, and circulated the influx out using the Driller's Method with weighted kill mud.

root_cause: Keyseat developed on the low side of the build section, and the drill pipe hung up while tripping out of the hole.
mitigation_applied: Reamed the tight spot, ran a keyseat wiper, and reduced tripping speed through the build section before continuing.

root_cause: Natural fracture network intersected while drilling ahead on a connection, causing an immediate reduction in returns at the shakers.
mitigation_applied: Stopped drilling and pumped a coarse LCM sweep, re-established returns, then resumed with reduced flow rate and a monitored pit level.

root_cause: Clay swelling and hole enlargement through a water-sensitive interval due to insufficient KCl inhibition in the water-based mud.
mitigation_applied: Raised KCl and polymer concentration, reduced open-hole exposure time, and back-reamed each connection until cavings at the shakers cleared.

mitigation_applied: Shut in, confirmed the influx by pit gain, and killed the well using the Wait and Weight method while holding casing pressure constant.
